annotationRationale: The distance formula and integer coordinate restrictions give universal chord bounds. The antipodal point supplies the upper bound, and a four-point construction attains both bounds while satisfying irrationality.
sourceMethod: Followed the official shortest-chord and antipodal-distance argument. Made the complementary squared-distance identity and simultaneous attainment by four distinct points explicit.

review.mathCheck: An irrational chord has two nonzero integer coordinate differences, giving RS²≥2. For the antipode T of P, either zero coordinate difference between T and Q would make PQ horizontal, vertical, or a diameter, all rational. Hence TQ²≥2 and PQ²+TQ²=100 gives PQ²≤98. The four supplied distinct points attain both bounds, so the maximum ratio is 7, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA Solution 17 across pages 5–6. It preserves the minimum-chord and antipodal maximum-chord approach while supplying the squared-distance identity and verifying simultaneous attainment.
review.annotationCheck: All four nodes match the worked method. Omitting enumeration of every lattice point is valid because the bounds apply universally and the attaining coordinates are verified.
